13	-module(json_rpc_dispatcher).
14	
15	-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").
16	
17	-export([
18	    dispatch/1,
19	    create_error_response/3,
20	    create_error_response/4,
21	    call_id_for_error/1
22	]).
23	
24	-type id() :: binary() | integer() | float() | null.
25	-type reply() :: no_response | map() | [map()].

27	-export_type([id/0, reply/0]).

29	%% @doc Dispatch a parsed JSON-RPC payload (single request or batch). Looks
30	%% each method up in the `json_rpc_methods' ETS registry. Returns either
31	%% `no_response' (for notifications and all-notification batches) or an Erlang
32	%% term ready to be jiffy-encoded.
33	-spec dispatch(term()) -> reply().
34	dispatch([]) ->
35	    create_error_response(null, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>);
36	dispatch(Requests) when is_list(Requests) ->
37	    Responses = [process_single_request(R) || R <- Requests],
38	    case [R || R <- Responses, R =/= no_response] of
39	        [] -> no_response;
40	        Filtered -> Filtered
41	    end;
42	dispatch(Request) when is_map(Request), map_size(Request) == 0 ->
43	    create_error_response(null, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>);
44	dispatch(Request) when is_map(Request) ->
45	    process_single_request(Request);
46	dispatch(_Request) ->
47	    create_error_response(null, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>).
48	
49	%% Internal
50	
51	process_single_request(Request) when is_map(Request) ->
52	    %% Extract the id best-effort first so a per-element envelope error can
53	    %% still echo the request id back to the client. extract_call_id/1
54	    %% returns 'notification' (id absent), null/binary/integer/float (valid
55	    %% id), or {error, invalid_id} (id present but not a permitted JSON
56	    %% type).
57	    case extract_call_id(Request) of
58	        {error, invalid_id} ->
59	            create_error_response(null, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>);
60	        Id ->
61	            case validate_envelope(Request) of
62	                {ok, Method} ->
63	                    case validate_params(Request) of
64	                        {ok, Params} ->
65	                            dispatch_method(Method, Params, Id);
66	                        {error, Code, Msg} ->
67	                            response_or_drop(
68	                                Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), Code, Msg)
69	                            )
70	                    end;
71	                {error, Code, Msg} ->
72	                    %% Envelope-level errors are not droppable as
73	                    %% notifications: the request was malformed, so we owe
74	                    %% the client an error envelope (with id: null when the
75	                    %% id was absent).
76	                    create_error_response(call_id(Id), Code, Msg)
77	            end
78	    end;
79	process_single_request(_) ->
80	    create_error_response(null, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>).
81	
82	validate_envelope(#{<<"jsonrpc">> := <<"2.0">>, <<"method">> := Method}) when
83	    is_binary(Method), Method =/= <<>>
84	->
85	    {ok, Method};
86	validate_envelope(_) ->
87	    {error, -32600, <<"Invalid Request">>}.
88	
89	validate_params(Request) ->
90	    case maps:find(<<"params">>, Request) of
91	        error ->
92	            {ok, []};
93	        {ok, Params} when is_list(Params); is_map(Params) ->
94	            {ok, Params};
95	        {ok, _} ->
96	            {error, -32602, <<"Invalid params">>}
97	    end.
98	
99	%% Returns the id for a call/notification:
100	%%   - missing key: notification (encoded internally as the atom 'notification')
101	%%   - present and one of String/Number/Null per spec: return verbatim
102	%%   - present but any other JSON type (boolean, array, object): {error, invalid_id}
103	extract_call_id(Request) ->
104	    case maps:find(<<"id">>, Request) of
105	        error -> notification;
106	        {ok, null} -> null;
107	        {ok, Id} when is_binary(Id) -> Id;
108	        {ok, Id} when is_integer(Id) -> Id;
109	        {ok, Id} when is_float(Id) -> Id;
110	        {ok, _} -> {error, invalid_id}
111	    end.
112	
113	dispatch_method(Method, Params, Id) ->
114	    case json_rpc_methods:lookup(Method) of
115	        not_found ->
116	            response_or_drop(
117	                Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), -32601, <<"Method not found">>)
118	            );
119	        {ok, {mfa, M, F}} ->
120	            invoke(fun() -> apply(M, F, [Params]) end, Id)
121	    end.
122	
123	invoke(Thunk, Id) ->
124	    try
125	        Result = Thunk(),
126	        case Id of
127	            notification -> no_response;
128	            _ -> create_result_response(Id, Result)
129	        end
130	    catch
131	        throw:{jsonrpc_error, Code, Msg} when is_integer(Code), is_binary(Msg) ->
132	            handle_thrown(Id, Code, Msg, no_data);
133	        throw:{jsonrpc_error, Code, Msg, Data} when is_integer(Code), is_binary(Msg) ->
134	            handle_thrown(Id, Code, Msg, {data, Data});
135	        %% Convert handler bugs (`error:_') and bare throws into a -32603
136	        %% envelope so a single misbehaving handler doesn't take down the
137	        %% connection. We deliberately do *not* catch `exit:_': an
138	        %% `exit/1' from a handler signals an unrecoverable failure that
139	        %% should propagate to `json_rpc_worker', which kills the worker
140	        %% process, returns `{error, {crash, exit, _}}' to the transport,
141	        %% and lets the transport reply with a generic Internal error.
142	        Class:Reason:Stacktrace when Class =:= error; Class =:= throw ->
143	            ?LOG_ERROR("Handler error: ~p:~p~n~p", [Class, Reason, Stacktrace]),
144	            response_or_drop(Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), -32603, <<"Internal error">>))
145	    end.
146	
147	%% A handler must use the application-defined error space. Reject any code in
148	%% the JSON-RPC reserved range -32768..-32000 — substituting -32603 Internal
149	%% error so the framework's own codes can't be impersonated by a handler.
150	handle_thrown(Id, Code, _Msg, _Data) when Code >= -32768, Code =< -32000 ->
151	    ?LOG_WARNING(
152	        "Handler threw reserved JSON-RPC error code ~p; substituting -32603", [Code]
153	    ),
154	    response_or_drop(Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), -32603, <<"Internal error">>));
155	handle_thrown(Id, Code, Msg, no_data) ->
156	    response_or_drop(Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), Code, Msg));
157	handle_thrown(Id, Code, Msg, {data, Data}) ->
158	    response_or_drop(Id, create_error_response(call_id(Id), Code, Msg, Data)).
159	
160	response_or_drop(notification, _Response) -> no_response;
161	response_or_drop(_Id, Response) -> Response.
162	
163	call_id(notification) -> null;
164	call_id(Id) -> Id.
165	
166	create_result_response(Id, Result) ->
167	    #{
168	        jsonrpc => <<"2.0">>,
169	        result => Result,
170	        id => Id
171	    }.
172	
173	-spec create_error_response(id(), integer(), binary()) -> map().
174	create_error_response(Id, Code, Message) ->
175	    #{
176	        jsonrpc => <<"2.0">>,
177	        error => #{code => Code, message => Message},
178	        id => Id
179	    }.
180	
181	-spec create_error_response(id(), integer(), binary(), term()) -> map().
182	create_error_response(Id, Code, Message, Data) ->
183	    #{
184	        jsonrpc => <<"2.0">>,
185	        error => #{code => Code, message => Message, data => Data},
186	        id => Id
187	    }.
188	
189	%% Best-effort id extraction from a parsed JSON-RPC payload, used by the
190	%% transport layers when synthesising a timeout/crash error envelope. For a
191	%% single-call object whose `id' is one of the JSON types permitted by the
192	%% spec (string/number/null) we echo it back so the client can correlate the
193	%% error to the originating request. For batches and any other shape we fall
194	%% back to `null' — there is no single id to attribute the error to.
195	-spec call_id_for_error(term()) -> id().
196	call_id_for_error(Parsed) when is_map(Parsed) ->
197	    case maps:find(<<"id">>, Parsed) of
198	        {ok, Id} when is_binary(Id); is_integer(Id); is_float(Id); Id =:= null -> Id;
199	        _ -> null
200	    end;
201	call_id_for_error(_Parsed) ->
202	    null.

45	            ?LOG_ERROR("Unhandled HTTP handler error: ~p:~p~n~p", [Class, Reason, Stacktrace]),
46	            Body = jiffy:encode(
47	                json_rpc_dispatcher:create_error_response(null, -32603, <<"Internal error">>)
48	            ),
49	            ReqErr = cowboy_req:reply(500, ?JSON_HEADERS, Body, Req0),
50	            {ok, ReqErr, State}
51	    end.
52	
53	handle(Req0, State) ->
54	    case cowboy_req:method(Req0) of
55	        <<"POST">> ->
56	            handle_post(Req0, State);
57	        _ ->
58	            Req = cowboy_req:reply(
59	                405,
60	                #{<<"allow">> => <<"POST">>},
61	                <<>>,
62	                Req0
63	            ),
64	            {ok, Req, State}
65	    end.
66	
67	handle_post(Req0, State) ->
68	    case content_type_is_json(Req0) of
69	        true ->
70	            handle_json_post(Req0, State);
71	        false ->
72	            Req = cowboy_req:reply(415, #{}, <<>>, Req0),
73	            {ok, Req, State}
74	    end.
75	
76	handle_json_post(Req0, State) ->
77	    MaxBody = maps:get(max_body_bytes, State),
78	    case read_full_body(Req0, MaxBody, <<>>) of
79	        {ok, Body, Req1} ->
80	            handle_body(Body, Req1, State);
81	        {too_large, Req1} ->
82	            %% The body was rejected at the size cap before any parsing, so
83	            %% -32700 Parse error is wrong. Use -32600 Invalid Request and
84	            %% keep the 413 status code.
85	            Req = cowboy_req:reply(413, ?JSON_HEADERS, ?INVALID_REQUEST_BODY, Req1),
86	            {ok, Req, State}
87	    end.
88	
89	read_full_body(Req0, MaxBody, Acc) ->
90	    %% Read in chunks, capping accumulated size at MaxBody.
91	    ReadOpts = #{length => MaxBody, period => 5000},
92	    case cowboy_req:read_body(Req0, ReadOpts) of
93	        {ok, Data, Req1} ->
94	            Combined = <<Acc/binary, Data/binary>>,
95	            case byte_size(Combined) > MaxBody of
96	                true -> {too_large, Req1};
97	                false -> {ok, Combined, Req1}
98	            end;
99	        {more, Data, Req1} ->
100	            Combined = <<Acc/binary, Data/binary>>,
101	            case byte_size(Combined) > MaxBody of
102	                true -> {too_large, Req1};
103	                false -> read_full_body(Req1, MaxBody, Combined)
104	            end
105	    end.
106	
107	handle_body(Body, Req0, State) ->
108	    case decode_json(Body) of
109	        {ok, Parsed} ->
110	            Timeout = maps:get(handler_timeout_ms, State),
111	            case json_rpc_worker:run(Parsed, Timeout) of
112	                {ok, Reply} ->
113	                    send_reply(Reply, Req0, State);
114	                {error, timeout} ->
115	                    Id = json_rpc_dispatcher:call_id_for_error(Parsed),
116	                    ErrBody = jiffy:encode(
117	                        json_rpc_dispatcher:create_error_response(
118	                            Id, -32603, <<"Internal error">>, #{reason => timeout}
119	                        )
120	                    ),
121	                    Req = cowboy_req:reply(200, ?JSON_HEADERS, ErrBody, Req0),
122	                    {ok, Req, State};
123	                {error, {crash, Class, Reason}} ->
124	                    ?LOG_ERROR("Handler crashed: ~p:~p", [Class, Reason]),
125	                    Id = json_rpc_dispatcher:call_id_for_error(Parsed),
126	                    ErrBody = jiffy:encode(
127	                        json_rpc_dispatcher:create_error_response(
128	                            Id, -32603, <<"Internal error">>
129	                        )
130	                    ),
131	                    Req = cowboy_req:reply(200, ?JSON_HEADERS, ErrBody, Req0),
132	                    {ok, Req, State}
133	            end;
134	        {error, parse_error} ->
135	            Req = cowboy_req:reply(200, ?JSON_HEADERS, ?PARSE_ERROR_BODY, Req0),
136	            {ok, Req, State}
137	    end.
138	
139	decode_json(Body) ->
140	    try
141	        {ok, jiffy:decode(Body, [return_maps])}
142	    catch
143	        _:_ -> {error, parse_error}
144	    end.
145	
146	send_reply(no_response, Req0, State) ->
147	    Req = cowboy_req:reply(204, #{}, <<>>, Req0),
148	    {ok, Req, State};
149	send_reply(Reply, Req0, State) ->
150	    Body = jiffy:encode(Reply),
151	    Req = cowboy_req:reply(200, ?JSON_HEADERS, Body, Req0),
152	    {ok, Req, State}.
153	
154	content_type_is_json(Req) ->
155	    try cowboy_req:parse_header(<<"content-type">>, Req) of
156	        {<<"application">>, <<"json">>, _} -> true;
157	        _ -> false
158	    catch
159	        _:_ -> false
160	    end.

14	
15	-behaviour(cowboy_websocket).
16	
17	-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").
18	
19	-export([init/2, websocket_init/1, websocket_handle/2, websocket_info/2, terminate/3]).
20	
21	%% Pre-encoded constant parse-error envelope. The WS endpoint emits this
22	%% on any frame that fails JSON parsing; there is no request id to echo
23	%% and the body never varies. The exact byte sequence matches what
24	%% `jiffy:encode/1' produces for the equivalent map; see
25	%% `test_ws_malformed_json' for the round-trip assertion.
26	-define(PARSE_ERROR_BODY,
27	    <<"{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":null,\"error\":{\"message\":\"Parse error\",\"code\":-32700}}">>
28	).
29	
30	init(Req, _State) ->
31	    %% Accept the upgrade regardless of what (if any) subprotocols the
32	    %% client offers. RFC 6455 lets the server simply not select one — by
33	    %% omitting the `sec-websocket-protocol' response header — and many
34	    %% browser/SDK clients routinely advertise a subprotocol as a hint.
35	    %% Refusing the upgrade for that broke interop without buying anything.
36	    %%
37	    %% Snapshot config values once at upgrade so the per-frame hot path
38	    %% doesn't go back through `application:get_env' + the validator on
39	    %% every text frame. The Cowboy ws options use the same snapshot.
40	    MaxFrame = json_rpc_config:get(ws_max_frame_bytes),
41	    IdleTimeout = json_rpc_config:get(ws_idle_timeout_ms),
42	    HandlerTimeout = json_rpc_config:get(handler_timeout_ms),
43	    Opts = #{
44	        max_frame_size => MaxFrame,
45	        idle_timeout => IdleTimeout,
46	        compress => false
47	    },
48	    State = #{handler_timeout_ms => HandlerTimeout},
49	    {cowboy_websocket, Req, State, Opts}.
50	
51	websocket_init(State) ->
52	    %% Join the connection-wide drain group so the listener can broadcast a
53	    %% close request during shutdown. `pg' monitors members and removes
54	    %% them on exit, so no explicit cleanup in `terminate/3' is required.
55	    ok = pg:join(json_rpc, json_rpc_ws_connections, self()),
56	    {[], State}.
57	
58	websocket_handle({text, Frame}, State) ->
59	    case decode_json(Frame) of
60	        {ok, Parsed} ->
61	            Timeout = maps:get(handler_timeout_ms, State),
62	            case json_rpc_worker:run(Parsed, Timeout) of
63	                {ok, no_response} ->
64	                    {[], State};
65	                {ok, Reply} ->
66	                    {[{text, jiffy:encode(Reply)}], State};
67	                {error, timeout} ->
68	                    Id = json_rpc_dispatcher:call_id_for_error(Parsed),
69	                    ErrBody = jiffy:encode(
70	                        json_rpc_dispatcher:create_error_response(
71	                            Id, -32603, <<"Internal error">>, #{reason => timeout}
72	                        )
73	                    ),
74	                    {[{text, ErrBody}], State};
75	                {error, {crash, Class, Reason}} ->
76	                    ?LOG_ERROR("Handler crashed: ~p:~p", [Class, Reason]),
77	                    Id = json_rpc_dispatcher:call_id_for_error(Parsed),
78	                    ErrBody = jiffy:encode(
79	                        json_rpc_dispatcher:create_error_response(
80	                            Id, -32603, <<"Internal error">>
81	                        )
82	                    ),
83	                    {[{text, ErrBody}], State}
84	            end;
85	        {error, parse_error} ->
86	            {[{text, ?PARSE_ERROR_BODY}], State}
87	    end;
88	websocket_handle({binary, _Data}, State) ->
89	    %% JSON-RPC framing on WS is text-only. Close the connection with
90	    %% status 1003 (Unsupported Data) rather than silently dropping the
91	    %% frame, so a client that sends binary by mistake gets explicit
92	    %% feedback instead of a stalled stream.
93	    {[{close, 1003, <<"binary frames not supported">>}], State};
94	websocket_handle(_Frame, State) ->
95	    {[], State}.
96	
97	websocket_info({json_rpc_push, Frame}, State) ->
98	    %% Server-push delivery from `json_rpc_ws:push/3' or `publish/3'. The
99	    %% frame is already an encoded JSON-RPC Notification; emit it as a
100	    %% text frame.
101	    {[{text, Frame}], State};
102	websocket_info(json_rpc_drain, State) ->
103	    %% Listener is shutting down. Send a 1001 (Going Away) close frame so
104	    %% the client knows to reconnect elsewhere; Cowboy will tear the
105	    %% connection down once the close frame is flushed.
106	    {[{close, 1001, <<"server shutting down">>}], State};
107	websocket_info(_Info, State) ->
108	    {[], State}.
109	
110	terminate(_Reason, _Req, _State) ->
111	    ok.
112	
113	decode_json(Body) ->
114	    try
115	        {ok, jiffy:decode(Body, [return_maps])}
116	    catch
117	        _:_ -> {error, parse_error}
118	    end.

13	-module(json_rpc_worker).
14	
15	%% Spawn-monitor-await primitive that runs `json_rpc_dispatcher:dispatch/1'
16	%% in a short-lived worker process. The caller blocks for at most `Timeout'
17	%% milliseconds. On timeout the worker is killed and `{error, timeout}' is
18	%% returned; on a worker crash `{error, {crash, Class, Reason}}' is returned;
19	%% otherwise the dispatcher's reply is returned in `{ok, Reply}'.
20	
21	-export([run/2]).
22	
23	-spec run(Parsed :: term(), Timeout :: timeout()) ->
24	    {ok, json_rpc_dispatcher:reply()}
25	    | {error, timeout}
26	    | {error, {crash, Class :: atom(), Reason :: term()}}.
27	run(Parsed, Timeout) ->
28	    Caller = self(),
29	    {Pid, MRef} = spawn_monitor(fun() ->
30	        Reply = json_rpc_dispatcher:dispatch(Parsed),
31	        Caller ! {?MODULE, self(), Reply}
32	    end),
33	    receive
34	        {?MODULE, Pid, Reply} ->
35	            erlang:demonitor(MRef, [flush]),
36	            {ok, Reply};
37	        {'DOWN', MRef, process, Pid, Reason} ->
38	            {error, {crash, exit, Reason}}
39	    after Timeout ->
40	        exit(Pid, kill),
41	        receive
42	            {'DOWN', MRef, process, Pid, _} -> ok
43	        end,
44	        %% A late result message could already be in our mailbox if the
45	        %% worker delivered just before the kill landed; flush it.
46	        receive
47	            {?MODULE, Pid, _} -> ok
48	        after 0 -> ok
49	        end,
50	        {error, timeout}
51	    end.

17	-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").

20	-export([
21	    init/1,
22	    handle_call/3,
23	    handle_cast/2,
24	    handle_info/2,
25	    terminate/2,
26	    code_change/3
27	]).

30	
31	%%% Public API
32	
33	-spec start_link() -> {ok, pid()} | {error, term()}.
34	start_link() ->
35	    gen_server:start_link({local, ?MODULE}, ?MODULE, [], []).
36

38	
39	-spec init([]) -> {ok, map()} | {stop, term()}.
40	init([]) ->
41	    %% Trap exits so the supervisor's `shutdown' signal is delivered as a
42	    %% message and `terminate/2' runs the graceful drain logic instead of
43	    %% the process being killed outright.
44	    process_flag(trap_exit, true),
45	    Port = json_rpc_config:get(port),
46	    MaxBody = json_rpc_config:get(max_body_bytes),
47	    MaxConns = json_rpc_config:get(max_connections),
48	    NumAcceptors = json_rpc_config:get(num_acceptors),
49	    IdleTimeout = json_rpc_config:get(idle_timeout_ms),
50	    RequestTimeout = json_rpc_config:get(request_timeout_ms),
51	
52	    Dispatch = cowboy_router:compile([
53	        {'_', [
54	            {"/rpc", json_rpc_http_handler, #{max_body_bytes => MaxBody}},
55	            {"/ws", json_rpc_ws_handler, []}
56	        ]}
57	    ]),
58	    TransportOpts = #{
59	        socket_opts => [{port, Port}],
60	        num_acceptors => NumAcceptors,
61	        max_connections => MaxConns
62	    },
63	    ProtocolOpts = #{
64	        env => #{dispatch => Dispatch},
65	        idle_timeout => IdleTimeout,
66	        max_keepalive => infinity,
67	        request_timeout => RequestTimeout,
68	        %% Pin to HTTP/1.1: our `request_timeout' knob is HTTP/1.1-only,
69	        %% and silently accepting an h2c upgrade would leave the
70	        %% transport-level idle wait unset on HTTP/2 connections.
71	        protocols => [http]
72	    },
73	    case cowboy:start_clear(?LISTENER, TransportOpts, ProtocolOpts) of
74	        {ok, _ListenerPid} ->
75	            {ok, #{}};
76	        {error, Reason} ->
77	            {stop, Reason}
78	    end.
79	
80	handle_call(_Request, _From, State) ->
81	    {reply, {error, unknown_call}, State}.
82	
83	handle_cast(_Msg, State) ->
84	    {noreply, State}.
85	
86	handle_info(_Info, State) ->
87	    {noreply, State}.

89	%% Best-effort graceful shutdown: install a 503-replying dispatch so no new
90	%% work is accepted, ask every live WS handler to send a 1001 close frame,
91	%% then poll Ranch until in-flight connections drain (capped at
92	%% `drain_timeout_ms') and stop the listener. For stronger guarantees use a
93	%% load balancer that stops sending traffic before SIGTERM.
94	terminate(_Reason, _State) ->
95	    DrainMs = json_rpc_config:get(drain_timeout_ms),
96	    DrainDispatch = cowboy_router:compile([
97	        {'_', [{"/[...]", json_rpc_drain_handler, []}]}
98	    ]),
99	    _ = cowboy:set_env(?LISTENER, dispatch, DrainDispatch),
100	    broadcast_ws_drain(),
101	    Deadline = erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) + DrainMs,
102	    wait_drain(Deadline),
103	    _ = cowboy:stop_listener(?LISTENER),
104	    ok.
105	
106	code_change(_OldVsn, State, _Extra) ->
107	    {ok, State}.
108	
109	%%% Internal
110	
111	wait_drain(Deadline) ->
112	    case ranch:procs(?LISTENER, connections) of
113	        [] ->
114	            ok;
115	        _Pids ->
116	            case erlang:monotonic_time(millisecond) >= Deadline of
117	                true ->
118	                    ok;
119	                false ->
120	                    timer:sleep(50),
121	                    wait_drain(Deadline)
122	            end
123	    end.
124	
125	%% Send a `json_rpc_drain' message to every WS handler that joined the
126	%% drain group in `websocket_init/1'. Each handler responds by emitting a
127	%% 1001 close frame and exiting, which lets the wait_drain/1 poll above
128	%% reach an empty connection list quickly instead of relying on the
129	%% drain-deadline brutal-kill.
130	broadcast_ws_drain() ->
131	    try pg:get_members(json_rpc, json_rpc_ws_connections) of
132	        Pids ->
133	            lists:foreach(fun(Pid) -> Pid ! json_rpc_drain end, Pids)
134	    catch
135	        %% The pg scope may already be down (e.g. supervisor shutdown
136	        %% order). Treat that as "no WS handlers to notify"; the
137	        %% wait_drain poll still bounds total shutdown time.
138	        _:_ -> ok
139	    end.

13	-module(json_rpc_ws).
14	
15	%% Public server-push API for the WebSocket transport. JSON-RPC 2.0 is
16	%% peer-symmetric, so the server is allowed to send Notification objects
17	%% (no `id' member) on its own initiative. This module exposes:
18	%%
19	%%   - `push/3'        — send a Notification to one specific connection.
20	%%   - `subscribe/2'   — join a connection to a topic.
21	%%   - `unsubscribe/2' — leave a topic.
22	%%   - `publish/3'     — broadcast a Notification to every subscriber of a
23	%%                       topic.
24	%%
25	%% Subscriptions are backed by `pg' in the `json_rpc' scope. `pg' monitors
26	%% its members, so when a WS handler process exits its subscriptions are
27	%% cleaned up automatically — no `terminate/3' hook needed.
28	%%
29	%% Distributed caveat: `pg' is local to this Erlang node by default. To fan
30	%% out across replicas either cluster the BEAM nodes (e.g. libcluster against
31	%% a headless Kubernetes service) so `pg' joins span the cluster, or bridge
32	%% to an external bus (Redis, NATS, Kafka, …) from each node and translate
33	%% inbound bus messages into local `publish/3' calls. This library does not
34	%% ship a bus bridge.
35	
36	-export([
37	    push/3,
38	    subscribe/2,
39	    unsubscribe/2,
40	    publish/3
41	]).
42	
43	-define(SCOPE, json_rpc).
44	
45	-type topic() :: term().
46	
47	-export_type([topic/0]).
48	
49	%% @doc Send a JSON-RPC Notification (a request without an `id' member) to a
50	%% single WS connection. The frame is delivered to the connection process
51	%% via `{json_rpc_push, Frame}'; the WS handler turns that into a text
52	%% frame.
53	-spec push(pid(), binary(), term()) -> ok.
54	push(ConnPid, Method, Params) when is_pid(ConnPid), is_binary(Method) ->
55	    Frame = encode_notification(Method, Params),
56	    ConnPid ! {json_rpc_push, Frame},
57	    ok.
58	
59	%% @doc Join `ConnPid' to the `pg' group identified by `Topic'. Idempotent;
60	%% `pg' tolerates multiple joins of the same pid.
61	-spec subscribe(pid(), topic()) -> ok.
62	subscribe(ConnPid, Topic) when is_pid(ConnPid) ->
63	    pg:join(?SCOPE, group_name(Topic), ConnPid).
64	
65	%% @doc Remove `ConnPid' from the `pg' group identified by `Topic'. Returns
66	%% `ok' even if the pid was not a member.
67	-spec unsubscribe(pid(), topic()) -> ok.
68	unsubscribe(ConnPid, Topic) when is_pid(ConnPid) ->
69	    case pg:leave(?SCOPE, group_name(Topic), ConnPid) of
70	        ok -> ok;
71	        not_joined -> ok
72	    end.
73	
74	%% @doc Broadcast a JSON-RPC Notification to every connection currently
75	%% subscribed to `Topic'. Encoding happens once; each subscriber receives
76	%% the same frame.
77	-spec publish(topic(), binary(), term()) -> ok.
78	publish(Topic, Method, Params) when is_binary(Method) ->
79	    Frame = encode_notification(Method, Params),
80	    Members = pg:get_members(?SCOPE, group_name(Topic)),
81	    lists:foreach(
82	        fun(Pid) -> Pid ! {json_rpc_push, Frame} end,
83	        Members
84	    ),
85	    ok.
86	
87	%% Internal
88	
89	group_name(Topic) ->
90	    {json_rpc_topic, Topic}.
91	
92	encode_notification(Method, Params) ->
93	    Notification = notification_object(Method, Params),
94	    jiffy:encode(Notification).
95	
96	%% Per the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec, `params' is an OPTIONAL member; omit it
97	%% entirely when the caller passes `undefined' so we don't ship a
98	%% `"params": null' object that some clients reject.
99	notification_object(Method, undefined) ->
100	    #{jsonrpc => <<"2.0">>, method => Method};
101	notification_object(Method, Params) ->
102	    #{jsonrpc => <<"2.0">>, method => Method, params => Params}.

26	    %% LOST. The embedding application is responsible for re-registering its

28	    %% SIGTERM/restart signal in its own startup code, or by seeding the
29	    %% registry from app config in its own supervisor's init).
30	    SupFlags = #{strategy => rest_for_one, intensity => 5, period => 10},
31	    DrainMs = json_rpc_config:get(drain_timeout_ms),
32	    %% The listener's terminate/2 may take up to drain_timeout_ms; give the
33	    %% supervisor enough budget to wait for it to finish before brutal-killing.

35	    Children = [
36	        #{
37	            id => json_rpc_methods,
38	            start => {json_rpc_methods, start_link, []},
39	            restart => permanent,
40	            shutdown => 5000,
41	            type => worker,
42	            modules => [json_rpc_methods]
43	        },
44	        %% A `pg' scope is itself a process. Start it before the listener
45	        %% so the WS handlers can join groups (for server-push) and the
46	        %% drain group as soon as they accept a connection. If the scope

1	# json-rpc
2	
3	[JSON-RPC-2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) server in Erlang, exposed
4	over plain HTTP and WebSocket via [Cowboy](https://github.com/ninenines/cowboy).
5	
6	## Endpoints
7	
8	The application starts a single Cowboy listener with two routes:
9	
10	| Route          | Method | Purpose                              |
11	|----------------|--------|--------------------------------------|
12	| `POST /rpc`    | POST   | One-shot JSON-RPC call/notification/batch. |
13	| `GET /ws`      | GET    | Persistent JSON-RPC channel over WebSocket text frames. |
14	
15	The HTTP transport answers with `200 OK` for any well-formed JSON-RPC payload —
16	JSON-RPC errors live in the response body, not the HTTP status. The transport
17	layer itself returns:
18	
19	- `204 No Content` for notifications and all-notification batches (no body).
20	- `405 Method Not Allowed` (with `Allow: POST`) for non-`POST` requests to `/rpc`.
21	- `413 Payload Too Large` (with a `-32700` JSON-RPC body) when the request body
22	  exceeds `max_body_bytes`.
23	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` when `Content-Type` is not `application/json`.
24	
25	The WebSocket endpoint accepts JSON-RPC payloads as text frames and responds
26	with text frames (notifications produce no frame at all). Malformed JSON
27	yields a `-32700` envelope as a text frame.
28	
29	## Usage
30	
31	### Register a method
32	
33	```erlang
34	ok = json_rpc_methods:register_method(
35	    <<"subtract">>,
36	    {my_handlers, subtract}
37	).
38	```
39	
40	Handlers are `{Module, Function}` pairs invoked as arity-1 (the function
41	receives the JSON-RPC `params` value). They may surface application-level
42	errors by throwing the structured tuple `{jsonrpc_error, Code, Msg}` or
43	`{jsonrpc_error, Code, Msg, Data}`; the values flow through to the JSON-RPC
44	`error` object verbatim.
45	
46	### HTTP examples
47	
48	A call:
49	
50	```sh
51	curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/rpc \
52	    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
53	    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"subtract","params":[42,23],"id":1}'
54	# -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":19,"id":1}
55	```
56	
57	A notification (no `id` member, expect `204 No Content`):
58	
59	```sh
60	curl -sS -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/rpc \
61	    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
62	    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"update","params":[1,2,3]}'
63	# -> HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
64	```
65	
66	A batch (notifications inside a batch are silently dropped from the response
67	array; an all-notification batch yields `204 No Content`):
68	
69	```sh
70	curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/rpc \
71	    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
72	    -d '[
73	        {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"sum","params":[1,2,4],"id":"1"},
74	        {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notify_hello","params":[7]},
75	        {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"subtract","params":[42,23],"id":"2"}
76	    ]'
77	# -> [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":7,"id":"1"},
78	#     {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":19,"id":"2"}]
79	```
80	
81	## Configuration
82	
83	Set these via `application:set_env/3` (or `sys.config`) before
84	`application:ensure_all_started(json_rpc)`.
85	
86	| Key                | Default       | Meaning |
87	|--------------------|---------------|---------|
88	| `port`             | `8080`        | TCP port for the Cowboy listener. |
89	| `max_body_bytes`   | `1_048_576`   | Per-request body cap. Overflow → `413` with a `-32700` body. |
90	| `max_connections`  | `1_024`       | `ranch`'s `max_connections` for the listener. |
91	| `num_acceptors`    | `10`          | Number of acceptor processes. |
92	| `idle_timeout_ms`  | `60_000`      | Cowboy `idle_timeout` (applies to keep-alive HTTP and WebSocket). |
93	
94	## Securing your endpoint
95	
96	The library ships **no** authentication, no TLS listener, and no `Authorization`
97	parsing of any kind. By design it expects to sit plaintext behind an L7 proxy
98	(Envoy, nginx, HAProxy, …) that terminates TLS, enforces rate limits, and
99	applies whatever auth scheme you use (mTLS, bearer tokens, OIDC, …). If you
100	need to authenticate inside the BEAM, slot a Cowboy middleware in front of the
101	two handlers; full recipes will land in a later phase.
102	
103	## Development
104	
105	`erlang` and `rebar3` are the two required development dependencies; `erlfmt` is useful but not mandatory. There is a [`flake.nix`](./flake.nix) with a development shell with both dependencies present, you can run the shell with `nix develop` (you may want to pass `--command /bin/zsh` on macOS), or via `make sh`.
106	
107	There is a [`Makefile`](./Makefile) with the common tasks; run `make` to see
108	them:
109	
110	```
111	Run tasks for json-rpc
112	
113	  build      compile the json-rpc application
114	  clean      run rebar3 clean and delete the build dir
115	  deps       get dependencies for the project
116	  format     run the erlfmt formatter
117	  lint       run linter (rebar3_lint)
118	  xref       run rebar3 xref
119	  dialyzer   run rebar3 dialyzer
120	  check      run format, lint, xref, dialyzer (fail fast)
121	  test       run all common_test suites
122	  ct         run rebar3 ct
123	  sh         launch a nix shell with zsh (erlang, rebar3)
124	```
125	
126	Alternatively, you can use `rebar3` directly.
127	
128	|Command|Description|
129	|-|-|
130	|`rebar3 update`|Download any dependencies|
131	|`rebar3 compile`|Build the project|
132	|`rebar3 ct`|Run all common_test suites|
133	|`rebar3 xref`|Run cross-reference checks|
134	|`rebar3 dialyzer`|Run the static type analyzer|
135	|`rebar3 format`|Run the [Erlang formatter](https://github.com/WhatsApp/erlfmt)|

13	-module(json_rpc_test_methods).
14	
15	-export([
16	    subtract/1,
17	    sum/1,
18	    get_data/1,
19	    update/1,
20	    notify_sum/1,
21	    notify_hello/1,
22	    throw_error/1,
23	    throw_reserved_error/1,
24	    slow/1,
25	    crash/1,
26	    crash_exit/1
27	]).
28	
29	subtract([A, B]) -> A - B.
30	
31	sum([A, B, C]) -> A + B + C.
32	
33	get_data(_) -> [<<"hello">>, 5].
34	
35	update(_) -> ok.
36	
37	notify_sum(_) -> ok.
38	
39	notify_hello(_) -> ok.
40	
41	throw_error(_) ->
42	    throw({jsonrpc_error, -1, <<"bad arg">>, #{<<"detail">> => <<"oops">>}}).
43	
44	%% A handler attempting to impersonate a framework-reserved error code. The
45	%% dispatcher must intercept this and substitute -32603 Internal error.
46	throw_reserved_error(_) ->
47	    throw({jsonrpc_error, -32601, <<"fake method not found">>}).
48	
49	%% Sleeps for the number of milliseconds passed as a single positional param.
50	slow([Ms]) when is_integer(Ms), Ms >= 0 ->
51	    timer:sleep(Ms),
52	    <<"done">>.
53	
54	%% Raises an `error' exception so the dispatcher's surrounding try/catch
55	%% converts it into a -32603 Internal error envelope. Used to verify that
56	%% the dispatcher's narrowed catch still handles handler bugs gracefully.
57	crash(_) ->
58	    error(boom).
59	
60	%% Calls `exit/1' so the exception is not caught by the dispatcher and
61	%% propagates to `json_rpc_worker', which kills the worker process and
62	%% returns `{error, {crash, exit, boom}}' to the transport. Used to verify
63	%% that the per-request worker isolates real handler crashes from the
64	%% connection process.
65	crash_exit(_) ->
66	    exit(boom).

267	%% POST a JSON-RPC payload (already encoded as a binary) to /rpc and return
268	%% {Status, Headers, Body} where Body is the raw response body.
269	raw_post(Conn, Payload) ->
270	    raw_post(Conn, Payload, ?JSON_HEADERS).

272	raw_post(Conn, Payload, Headers) ->
273	    StreamRef = gun:post(Conn, "/rpc", Headers, Payload),
274	    case gun:await(Conn, StreamRef, 5000) of
275	        {response, fin, Status, RespHeaders} ->
276	            {Status, RespHeaders, <<>>};
277	        {response, nofin, Status, RespHeaders} ->
278	            {ok, Body} = gun:await_body(Conn, StreamRef, 5000),
279	            {Status, RespHeaders, Body}
280	    end.

282	%% Issue a JSON-RPC call/notification/batch as an Erlang term, return the
283	%% decoded JSON-RPC envelope (or no_response for 204s).
284	rpc_call(Conn, Term) ->
285	    Payload = jiffy:encode(Term),
286	    case raw_post(Conn, Payload) of
287	        {204, _Hs, _} ->
288	            no_response;
289	        {200, _Hs, Body} ->
290	            jiffy:decode(Body, [return_maps])
291	    end.

1	# Production-Readiness Plan
2	
3	Tracks the remaining work to take `json_rpc` to a 1.0 release.
4	
5	Already merged: project hygiene, JSON-RPC 2.0 spec compliance,
6	HTTP + WebSocket transport via Cowboy, ETS-backed registry under
7	hardened supervision, a focused spec-compliance touch-up pass
8	(strict `id` validation, oversize-body code, reserved-range guard
9	on handler-thrown errors), per-request worker processes for handler
10	dispatch with timeout + crash isolation, dispatcher correctness
11	fixes (per-element `id` preservation, narrowed exception catch),
12	the WebSocket server-push API (`push`/`subscribe`/`publish` on
13	`pg`) plus WS hardening (subprotocol acceptance, bounded frame
14	size, explicit idle timeout, binary-frame closure, id-preserving
15	error envelopes, graceful WS drain), and a focused cleanup pass
16	(ETS table now `protected`, dropped deprecated raw-fun handler
17	support, split `request_timeout_ms` into `handler_timeout_ms` +
18	`request_timeout_ms`, lowered `num_acceptors` to Ranch's default
19	of 10, pinned Cowboy to HTTP/1.1, honest `rest_for_one` doc note,
20	several dead-code drops, pre-encoded constant error envelopes,
21	hot-path config snapshotted at handler init).
22	
23	## Locked-in architectural decisions
24	
25	These are baked in. Don't re-litigate without explicit go-ahead.
26	
27	- **HTTP + WebSocket only.** No raw TCP / NDJSON / other transports.
28	- **No auth, no TLS in the library.** Sits plaintext behind an L7
29	  proxy (Envoy / nginx / ALB) which terminates TLS and handles auth.
30	  The HTTP client (Phase 9) accepts arbitrary headers at construction
31	  so callers can attach `Authorization` themselves; the library
32	  never inspects them.
33	- **Method handlers stored as `{Module, Function}` MFAs.** The raw
34	  `fun/1` overload was removed in the cleanup pass.
35	- **Method registry in ETS, owned by `json_rpc_methods` gen_server.**
36	  Writes go through the gen_server; reads go directly to ETS for
37	  read concurrency. Table is `protected` — only the gen_server can
38	  write.
39	- **`json_rpc_sup` uses `rest_for_one`** with `pg` scope first, then
40	  registry, then listener. NOTE: registry crash → empty table on
41	  restart. The embedding application is responsible for re-
42	  registering its method set after a registry crash.
43	- **Defaults live in the `env` block of `src/json_rpc.app.src`.**
44	  `src/json_rpc_config.erl` validates them at boot via
45	  `validate_all/0`. Two timeout keys: `handler_timeout_ms` is the
46	  worker handler-execution deadline; `request_timeout_ms` is
47	  Cowboy's transport-level idle wait between requests on a
48	  keep-alive connection.
49	- **Per-request handler dispatch runs in a monitored worker** via
50	  `json_rpc_worker:run/2`. The dispatcher catches `error` and
51	  `throw` and converts them to `-32603`; `exit/1` propagates to the
52	  worker so the worker isolation is meaningful.
53	- **WebSocket server-push via `pg`** (in OTP, no extra dependency).
54	  `pg` is local to the Erlang node — README will document the
55	  cluster / external-bus options for cross-replica fan-out.

87	## Phase 9 — HTTP and WebSocket clients
88	
89	The library currently ships no client. Tests use `gun` directly.
90	This phase ships a real client API.
91	
92	### HTTP client
93	
94	- [ ] `json_rpc_http_client` module backed by `gun`. API:
95	      `open/2`, `call/3`, `call/4` (with timeout), `notify/3`,
96	      `batch/2`, `close/1`.
97	- [ ] Auto-generate ids (monotonic integer); allow caller-supplied
98	      id as an override.
99	- [ ] Per-call timeout; surface `{error, timeout}` cleanly.
100	- [ ] Connection keep-alive / pool (gun handles this; expose pool
101	      size).
102	- [ ] Accept arbitrary request headers at construction (so callers
103	      can attach `Authorization` or anything else without the
104	      library knowing or caring).
105	
106	### WebSocket client
107	
108	- [ ] `json_rpc_ws_client` as a `gen_server` using `gun` for the WS
109	      connection. State: `pending = #{Id => From}`, `next_id`,
110	      `buffer`, `subscriber`.
111	- [ ] Demultiplex responses by `id`; `gen_server:reply/2` to the
112	      waiting caller.
113	- [ ] Per-call timeout; on timeout, drop the pending entry and
114	      return `{error, timeout}`.
115	- [ ] `batch/2` sends a single JSON array (notifications and calls
116	      together); honour the all-notifications-no-response rule.
117	- [ ] Reconnect with exponential backoff; in-flight callers get
118	      `{error, disconnected}` on socket close. Replay is out of
119	      scope — JSON-RPC has no idempotency semantics, so the caller
120	      decides whether to retry.
121	- [ ] Subscriber callback for server-pushed notifications: either
122	      `{notification, Method, Params}` messages to a caller pid or a
123	      configurable callback fun. Wires up against the Phase 7 push
124	      API end-to-end.

137	## Phase 10 — Limits and observability

142	### Limits
143	
144	- [ ] Add `max_batch_size` to `json_rpc_config` (default `100`).

146	      Request` body and HTTP `200`.
147	- [ ] **Per-call timeout enforcement inside batches.** Today the
148	      worker timeout applies to the whole batch; one slow element
149	      can blank-id-out the entire response. Enforce the configured
150	      `handler_timeout_ms` per element so a slow call doesn't poison
151	      its peers. Land alongside `max_batch_size`.
152	- [ ] **Cap HTTP keep-alive request count.** Add
153	      `max_keepalive_requests` (default ~1000) and pass it through

19	is on a request path where an exception would cost more than an error return
20	— a handler that returns a term JSON cannot represent must degrade to a
21	`-32603` envelope, not tear down the caller's connection. So this module
22	wraps both directions and returns tagged tuples instead.
23	
24	Using stdlib `json` rather than a third-party encoder also means the library
25	carries no native (NIF) dependency.
26	""".

31	    decode/1

37

39	validated by attempting to encode them, not by a type check.
40	""".

17	
18	An error object is a map with a `code`, a human-readable `message`, and an
19	optional `data` member carrying anything JSON-encodable:

23	```

26	the handler function or by raising one with `throw_error/2,3`. Both accept
27	the same shapes.

30	
31	The specification reserves `-32768..-32000`, but delegates `-32099..-32000`
32	to the implementation as "server errors". This library follows that split:
33	a handler may emit any code outside `-32768..-32100`, which includes the
34	whole `-32099..-32000` server-error range as well as all application-defined
35	codes. A handler that tries to emit a framework-owned code (`-32700`,
36	`-32600`, `-32601`, `-32602`, `-32603`, or anything else in

13	-module(json_rpc_response).
14	
15	-moduledoc """
16	Construction of JSON-RPC 2.0 Response objects.
17	
18	A Response is either a Result (`result` member present) or an Error
19	(`error` member present) — never both. Both always carry `jsonrpc` and `id`.
20	Notifications produce no Response at all, represented here as
21	`no_response`.
22	""".
23	
24	-include("json_rpc.hrl").
25	
26	-export([
27	    result/2,
28	    error/2,
29	    error/3,
30	    error/4
31	]).
32	
33	-doc """
34	The `id` of a Request, as constrained by the specification: a String, a
35	Number, or Null. `notification` is the internal marker for a Request with no
36	`id` member at all.
37	""".
38	-type id() :: binary() | integer() | float() | null.
39	
40	-doc "A Response object, ready to be encoded.".
41	-type t() :: #{
42	    jsonrpc := binary(),
43	    id := id(),
44	    result => json_rpc_json:value(),
45	    error => json_rpc_error:t()
46	}.
47	
48	-export_type([id/0, t/0]).
49	
50	-doc "Build a successful Response echoing `Id` and carrying `Result`.".
51	-spec result(id(), json_rpc_json:value()) -> t().
52	result(Id, Result) ->
53	    #{jsonrpc => ?JSONRPC_VERSION, id => Id, result => Result}.
54	
55	-doc "Build an error Response from an existing error object.".
56	-spec error(id(), json_rpc_error:t()) -> t().
57	error(Id, Error) when is_map(Error) ->
58	    #{jsonrpc => ?JSONRPC_VERSION, id => Id, error => Error}.
59	
60	-doc "Build an error Response from a code and message.".
61	-spec error(id(), json_rpc_error:code(), json_rpc_error:message()) -> t().
62	error(Id, Code, Message) ->
63	    error(Id, json_rpc_error:new(Code, Message)).
64	
65	-doc "Build an error Response from a code, message, and `data` member.".
66	-spec error(id(), json_rpc_error:code(), json_rpc_error:message(), json_rpc_error:data()) ->
67	    t().
68	error(Id, Code, Message, Data) ->
69	    error(Id, json_rpc_error:new(Code, Message, Data)).

13	-module(json_rpc_request).
14	
15	-moduledoc """
16	Validation of a single decoded JSON-RPC 2.0 Request object.
17	
18	`parse/1` turns one decoded JSON value into exactly one of three shapes:
19	
20	- `{call, Id, Method, Params}` — a well-formed Request that expects a
21	  Response.
22	- `{notification, Method, Params}` — a well-formed Request with no `id`
23	  member. It must never be answered, whatever the handler does.
24	- `{invalid, Id, Error}` — not a valid Request object. This *is* answered,
25	  even when no `id` was present, in which case `Id` is `null`. That follows
26	  the specification's own worked example, where an object carrying a
27	  non-string `method` and no `id` still draws an `-32600` response.
28	
29	The distinction matters: only a Request that survives validation can claim
30	the silence a Notification is entitled to.
31	""".
32	
33	-include("json_rpc.hrl").
34	
35	-export([parse/1, id_for_error/1]).
36	
37	-doc "The `params` member: by-position, by-name, or absent (`[]`).".
38	-type params() :: [json_rpc_json:value()] | #{binary() => json_rpc_json:value()}.
39	
40	-doc "The result of validating one Request object.".
41	-type parsed() ::
42	    {call, json_rpc_response:id(), binary(), params()}
43	    | {notification, binary(), params()}
44	    | {invalid, json_rpc_response:id(), json_rpc_error:t()}.
45	
46	-export_type([params/0, parsed/0]).
47	
48	-doc """
49	Validate one decoded Request object.
50	
51	Extraction is deliberately ordered so that a request carrying a usable `id`
52	gets that `id` echoed back on the error, even when the rest of the envelope
53	is malformed — otherwise a client cannot correlate the failure with the call
54	that caused it.
55	""".
56	-spec parse(json_rpc_json:value()) -> parsed().
57	parse(Request) when is_map(Request), map_size(Request) > 0 ->
58	    case extract_id(Request) of
59	        {error, invalid_id} ->
60	            %% An `id' of the wrong JSON type is not something we can echo,
61	            %% so the error carries `null'.
62	            {invalid, null, json_rpc_error:invalid_request()};
63	        Id ->
64	            parse_envelope(Request, Id)
65	    end;
66	parse(_Request) ->
67	    {invalid, null, json_rpc_error:invalid_request()}.
68	
69	-doc """
70	Best-effort `id` extraction for errors raised before or outside validation.
71	
72	Used by the transports when they have to answer a payload they could not
73	dispatch. A batch has no single `id` to attribute an error to, so it yields
74	`null`.
75	""".
76	-spec id_for_error(json_rpc_json:value()) -> json_rpc_response:id().
77	id_for_error(Payload) when is_map(Payload) ->
78	    case extract_id(Payload) of
79	        {error, invalid_id} -> null;
80	        notification -> null;
81	        Id -> Id
82	    end;
83	id_for_error(_Payload) ->
84	    null.
85	
86	%%% Internal
87	
88	parse_envelope(Request, Id) ->
89	    case Request of
90	        #{<<"jsonrpc">> := ?JSONRPC_VERSION, <<"method">> := Method} when
91	            is_binary(Method), Method =/= <<>>
92	        ->
93	            parse_params(Request, Id, Method);
94	        _ ->
95	            {invalid, echo(Id), json_rpc_error:invalid_request()}
96	    end.
97	
98	parse_params(Request, Id, Method) ->
99	    case maps:find(<<"params">>, Request) of
100	        error ->
101	            request(Id, Method, []);
102	        {ok, Params} when is_list(Params); is_map(Params) ->
103	            request(Id, Method, Params);
104	        {ok, _Other} ->
105	            %% `params' must be a structured value. A Request that violates
106	            %% that is not a valid Request object, so it is answered even
107	            %% when it carries no `id'.
108	            {invalid, echo(Id), json_rpc_error:invalid_params()}
109	    end.
110	
111	request(notification, Method, Params) ->
112	    {notification, Method, Params};
113	request(Id, Method, Params) ->
114	    {call, Id, Method, Params}.
115	
116	%% Absent `id' marks a Notification. Present, it must be a String, a Number,
117	%% or Null — booleans, arrays, and objects are rejected outright.
118	extract_id(Request) ->
119	    case maps:find(<<"id">>, Request) of
120	        error -> notification;
121	        {ok, null} -> null;
122	        {ok, Id} when is_binary(Id) -> Id;
123	        {ok, Id} when is_integer(Id) -> Id;
124	        {ok, Id} when is_float(Id) -> Id;
125	        {ok, _Other} -> {error, invalid_id}
126	    end.
127	
128	echo(notification) -> null;
129	echo(Id) -> Id.
130

13	-module(json_rpc_worker).
14	
15	-moduledoc """
16	Runs handler code in short-lived monitored processes under a deadline.
17	
18	Every handler invocation gets its own process. That buys three things the
19	connection process cannot provide on its own:
20	
21	- **A deadline.** A handler that blocks forever is killed at the timeout and
22	  reported as `{error, timeout}` instead of pinning the connection.
23	- **Crash isolation.** Any exception class, including `exit`, is contained;
24	  the caller gets `{error, {crash, ...}}` and stays healthy.
25	- **Heap isolation.** A handler that builds a large intermediate term has
26	  that garbage collected away with the process, rather than growing the
27	  long-lived connection process's heap.
28	
29	`run_many/2` runs a whole batch *concurrently* under a single shared
30	deadline. The specification explicitly permits processing a batch as a set
31	of concurrent tasks, and doing so bounds the worst case for a batch of N
32	slow calls at one timeout rather than N of them.
33	""".
34	
35	-export([run/2, run_many/2]).
36	
37	-doc "What became of one handler invocation.".
38	-type outcome() ::
39	    {ok, term()}
40	    | {error, timeout}
41	    | {error, {crash, Class :: error | exit | throw, Reason :: term(), erlang:stacktrace()}}.
42	
43	-doc "An outcome plus how long the invocation actually took, in microseconds.".
44	-type result() :: #{outcome := outcome(), duration := non_neg_integer()}.
45	
46	-export_type([outcome/0, result/0]).
47	
48	-define(TAG, '$json_rpc_worker').
49	
50	-doc """
51	Run a single function under `Timeout` milliseconds and return its outcome.
52	""".
53	-spec run(fun(() -> term()), timeout()) -> outcome().
54	run(Fun, Timeout) ->
55	    [#{outcome := Outcome}] = run_many([Fun], Timeout),
56	    Outcome.
57	
58	-doc """
59	Run every function concurrently under one shared `Timeout`.
60	
61	Results come back in the order the functions were given, regardless of the
62	order they finish in. Functions still running when the deadline passes are
63	killed and reported as `{error, timeout}`.
64	""".
65	-spec run_many([fun(() -> term())], timeout()) -> [result()].
66	run_many([], _Timeout) ->
67	    [];
68	run_many(Funs, Timeout) ->
69	    Started = erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond),
70	    Deadline = deadline(Started, Timeout),
71	    Pending = start_workers(Funs),
72	    Collected = collect(Pending, Deadline, #{}),
73	    Finished = erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond),
74	    [format(Index, Collected, Started, Finished) || Index <- lists:seq(1, length(Funs))].
75	
76	%%% Internal
77	
78	deadline(_Started, infinity) ->
79	    infinity;
80	deadline(Started, Timeout) when is_integer(Timeout), Timeout >= 0 ->
81	    Started + Timeout * 1000.
82	
83	%% #{Pid => {MonitorRef, Index}} for every worker still outstanding.
84	start_workers(Funs) ->
85	    Caller = self(),
86	    Indexed = lists:enumerate(Funs),
87	    maps:from_list([start_worker(Caller, Index, Fun) || {Index, Fun} <- Indexed]).
88	
89	start_worker(Caller, Index, Fun) ->
90	    {Pid, MonitorRef} = spawn_monitor(fun() ->
91	        Caller ! {?TAG, self(), guarded(Fun)}
92	    end),
93	    {Pid, {MonitorRef, Index}}.
94	
95	%% Catch every exception class inside the worker. Letting `exit' escape used
96	%% to be meaningful when the caller distinguished the two paths, but both
97	%% end up as the same `-32603' envelope, so containing everything here keeps
98	%% the reporting uniform and the stacktrace intact.
99	guarded(Fun) ->
100	    try
101	        {ok, Fun()}
102	    catch
103	        Class:Reason:Stacktrace -> {error, {crash, Class, Reason, Stacktrace}}
104	    end.
105	
106	collect(Pending, _Deadline, Acc) when map_size(Pending) =:= 0 ->
107	    Acc;
108	collect(Pending, Deadline, Acc) ->
109	    receive
110	        {?TAG, Pid, Outcome} when is_map_key(Pid, Pending) ->
111	            {{MonitorRef, Index}, Rest} = maps:take(Pid, Pending),
112	            erlang:demonitor(MonitorRef, [flush]),
113	            collect(Rest, Deadline, Acc#{Index => {Outcome, elapsed_now()}});
114	        {'DOWN', _MonitorRef, process, Pid, Reason} when is_map_key(Pid, Pending) ->
115	            %% The worker died without reporting: it was killed from the
116	            %% outside, or ran out of heap. `guarded/1' handles everything
117	            %% raised by the function itself.
118	            {{_Ref, Index}, Rest} = maps:take(Pid, Pending),
119	            Crash = {error, {crash, exit, Reason, []}},
120	            collect(Rest, Deadline, Acc#{Index => {Crash, elapsed_now()}})
121	    after time_left(Deadline) ->
122	        abandon(Pending, Acc)
123	    end.
124	
125	time_left(infinity) ->
126	    infinity;
127	time_left(Deadline) ->
128	    max(0, (Deadline - erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond) + 999) div 1000).
129	
130	elapsed_now() ->
131	    erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond).
132	
133	%% Kill everything still running and record it as a timeout. The DOWN is
134	%% guaranteed to arrive after `exit/2', and a result message may already be
135	%% in flight, so flush both.
136	abandon(Pending, Acc) ->
137	    maps:fold(
138	        fun(Pid, {MonitorRef, Index}, InnerAcc) ->
139	            exit(Pid, kill),
140	            receive
141	                {'DOWN', MonitorRef, process, Pid, _Reason} -> ok
142	            end,
143	            receive
144	                {?TAG, Pid, _Late} -> ok
145	            after 0 -> ok
146	            end,
147	            InnerAcc#{Index => {{error, timeout}, elapsed_now()}}
148	        end,
149	        Acc,
150	        Pending
151	    ).
152	
153	%% Timed-out entries are stamped when the deadline fired, which is the same
154	%% instant for all of them; completed entries carry their own finish time.
155	format(Index, Collected, Started, Finished) ->
156	    {Outcome, FinishedAt} = maps:get(Index, Collected, {{error, timeout}, Finished}),
157	    #{outcome => Outcome, duration => max(0, FinishedAt - Started)}.

13	-module(json_rpc_config).
14	
15	-moduledoc """
16	Validated access to the `json_rpc` application environment.
17	
18	There is no process here: every read goes through `application:get_env/2`
19	and is checked against the key's declared shape. Defaults live in the `env`
20	block of `json_rpc.app.src`, so `get/1` never has to invent one — an
21	unknown key is a programming error and raises `badarg`.
22	
23	`validate_all/0` runs at application start so a misconfigured node fails
24	immediately, with the offending key named, instead of crashing a listener
25	later with something less actionable.
26	
27	Reads are cheap but not free. Transport handlers snapshot the values they
28	need once at connection setup rather than calling `get/1` per request.
29	""".
30	
31	-compile({no_auto_import, [get/1]}).
32	
33	-export([get/1, keys/0, validate_all/0]).
34	
35	-doc "Every configuration key understood by the application.".
36	-type key() ::
37	    port
38	    | http_path
39	    | ws_path
40	    | max_body_bytes
41	    | max_connections
42	    | num_acceptors
43	    | idle_timeout_ms
44	    | request_timeout_ms
45	    | handler_timeout_ms
46	    | drain_timeout_ms
47	    | max_keepalive_requests
48	    | max_methods
49	    | max_batch_size
50	    | ws_max_frame_bytes
51	    | ws_idle_timeout_ms
52	    | ws_max_in_flight
53	    | methods.
54	
55	-export_type([key/0]).
56	
57	%% Declared shape of each key. `{integer, Min, Max}' bounds are inclusive.
58	-define(POS_INT, {integer, 1, infinity}).
59	-define(NON_NEG_INT, {integer, 0, infinity}).
60	
61	-doc "The list of keys `validate_all/0` walks. Ordered for readable errors.".
62	-spec keys() -> [key()].
63	keys() ->
64	    [
65	        port,
66	        http_path,
67	        ws_path,
68	        max_body_bytes,
69	        max_connections,
70	        num_acceptors,
71	        idle_timeout_ms,
72	        request_timeout_ms,
73	        handler_timeout_ms,
74	        drain_timeout_ms,
75	        max_keepalive_requests,
76	        max_methods,
77	        max_batch_size,
78	        ws_max_frame_bytes,
79	        ws_idle_timeout_ms,
80	        ws_max_in_flight,
81	        methods
82	    ].
83	
84	-doc """
85	Fetch a validated configuration value.
86	
87	Raises `badarg` for a key the application does not define, and
88	`{invalid_config, Key, Value, Reason}` for a defined key holding a value
89	that fails validation.
90	""".
91	-spec get(key()) -> term().
92	get(Key) ->
93	    case application:get_env(json_rpc, Key) of
94	        {ok, Value} -> validate(Key, Value);
95	        undefined -> erlang:error(badarg, [Key])
96	    end.
97	
98	-doc """
99	Validate every key, raising on the first bad one.
100	
101	Called from `json_rpc_app:start/2` so misconfiguration fails the application
102	start rather than a request.
103	""".
104	-spec validate_all() -> ok.
105	validate_all() ->
106	    lists:foreach(fun(Key) -> _ = get(Key) end, keys()),
107	    ok.
108	
109	%%% Internal
110	
111	%% The declared shape of each key, in one place so adding a knob is a
112	%% one-line change here plus a default in json_rpc.app.src.
113	shape(port) -> {integer, 1, 65535};
114	shape(http_path) -> path;
115	shape(ws_path) -> path;
116	shape(max_body_bytes) -> ?POS_INT;
117	shape(max_connections) -> ?POS_INT;
118	shape(num_acceptors) -> ?POS_INT;
119	shape(idle_timeout_ms) -> ?POS_INT;
120	shape(request_timeout_ms) -> ?POS_INT;
121	shape(handler_timeout_ms) -> ?POS_INT;
122	shape(drain_timeout_ms) -> ?NON_NEG_INT;
123	shape(max_keepalive_requests) -> ?POS_INT;
124	shape(max_methods) -> ?POS_INT;
125	shape(max_batch_size) -> ?POS_INT;
126	shape(ws_max_frame_bytes) -> ?POS_INT;
127	shape(ws_idle_timeout_ms) -> ?POS_INT;
128	shape(ws_max_in_flight) -> ?POS_INT;
129	shape(methods) -> method_list;
130	shape(_Other) -> unknown.
131	
132	validate(Key, Value) ->
133	    case shape(Key) of
134	        unknown -> erlang:error(badarg, [Key]);
135	        Shape -> check(Shape, Key, Value)
136	    end.
137	
138	check({integer, Min, Max}, Key, Value) when is_integer(Value) ->
139	    case Value >= Min andalso (Max =:= infinity orelse Value =< Max) of
140	        true -> Value;
141	        false -> bad(Key, Value, range_message(Min, Max))
142	    end;
143	check({integer, Min, Max}, Key, Value) ->
144	    bad(Key, Value, range_message(Min, Max));
145	%% Cowboy's router wants a string path; accept only absolute ones so a typo
146	%% shows up at boot instead of as a silent 404.
147	check(path, _Key, [$/ | _] = Value) ->
148	    Value;
149	check(path, Key, Value) ->
150	    bad(Key, Value, <<"must be an absolute path string, e.g. \"/rpc\"">>);
151	check(method_list, Key, Value) when is_list(Value) ->
152	    case lists:all(fun is_method_spec/1, Value) of
153	        true -> Value;
154	        false -> bad(Key, Value, <<"must be a list of {Name :: binary(), {Module, Function}}">>)
155	    end;
156	check(method_list, Key, Value) ->
157	    bad(Key, Value, <<"must be a list of {Name :: binary(), {Module, Function}}">>).
158	
159	is_method_spec({Name, {Module, Function}}) when
160	    is_binary(Name), is_atom(Module), is_atom(Function)
161	->
162	    true;
163	is_method_spec(_Other) ->
164	    false.
165	
166	range_message(Min, infinity) ->
167	    iolist_to_binary(io_lib:format("must be an integer >= ~p", [Min]));
168	range_message(Min, Max) ->
169	    iolist_to_binary(io_lib:format("must be an integer in ~p..~p", [Min, Max])).
170	
171	-spec bad(key(), term(), binary()) -> no_return().
172	bad(Key, Value, Reason) ->
173	    erlang:error({invalid_config, Key, Value, Reason}).

13	-module(json_rpc_methods).
14	
15	-moduledoc """
16	The method registry: a name-to-handler map backed by ETS.
17	
18	Writes go through this `m:gen_server` so validation and the size cap cannot
19	be raced. Reads go straight to the ETS table, which is `protected` and
20	configured for read concurrency — dispatch is the hot path and must not
21	queue behind a registration.
22	
23	## Handler arity
24	
25	A handler is a `{Module, Function}` pair. It is called with the request's
26	`params` as its only argument, or — if the module exports the same name at
27	arity 2 — with `params` and the request context (see
28	`t:json_rpc_dispatcher:context/0`). Arity 2 is preferred when both exist,
29	because a handler that wants the context has no other way to get it. The
30	export is checked at registration, so a typo fails immediately rather than
31	on the first call.
32	
33	## Surviving a restart
34	
35	If this process crashes, the table dies with it and `rest_for_one` restarts
36	the listener alongside it. Methods listed in the `methods` application
37	environment key are re-registered automatically on every start, so a
38	statically declared method set heals itself. Methods registered at runtime
39	do not: an application that registers dynamically should either declare them
40	in `methods` instead or re-register from its own supervision tree.
41	""".
42	
43	-behaviour(gen_server).
44	
45	-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").
46	
47	-export([
48	    start_link/0,
49	    register_method/2,
50	    unregister_method/1,
51	    lookup/1,
52	    list_methods/0,
53	    discover/1
54	]).
55	
56	-export([
57	    init/1,
58	    handle_call/3,
59	    handle_cast/2,
60	    handle_info/2,
61	    terminate/2,
62	    code_change/3
63	]).
64	
65	-define(TABLE, ?MODULE).
66	-define(BUILTIN_DISCOVER, <<"rpc.discover">>).
67	-define(CALL_TIMEOUT, 5000).
68	
69	-doc "A handler: a module and an exported function of arity 1 or 2.".
70	-type handler() :: {module(), atom()}.
71	
72	-doc "How a handler is stored, with the arity resolved at registration.".
73	-type stored_handler() :: {mfa, module(), atom(), 1 | 2}.

-module(json_rpc_dispatcher).

-moduledoc """
Routing of decoded JSON-RPC payloads to registered handlers.

Takes one already-decoded JSON value — a single Request object or a batch
array — and produces the Response term the transport should send back, or
`no_response` when the payload consisted only of Notifications.

## Batches

A batch is validated as a whole first: an empty array and an array longer
than `max_batch_size` are both `-32600 Invalid Request`, answered as a single
Response rather than an array. Otherwise every element is validated
independently, and the valid ones run **concurrently** under one shared
deadline. The specification explicitly allows processing a batch as a set of
concurrent tasks, and it means a batch of ten slow calls costs one timeout
rather than ten.

Responses come back in request order. Notifications contribute nothing to the
array, whatever their handler did or how badly it failed.

## Handler contract

A handler is called with the request's `params`, plus the context if it is
registered at arity 2. Its return value is interpreted as:

- `{error, Error}` — an error Response, where `Error` is anything
  `json_rpc_error:from_term/1` accepts.
- `{ok, Result}` — a successful Response carrying `Result`.
- any other term — a successful Response carrying that term.

`{ok, _}` and `{error, _}` are unambiguous as control tuples because a bare
tuple is not JSON-encodable, so no handler can want to return one as a result.

A handler may also raise, via `json_rpc_error:throw_error/2,3` for a
deliberate protocol error, or by crashing. A crash, a timeout, and a handler
that tries to claim a framework-reserved error code all become
`-32603 Internal error`; the real reason is logged and reported over
telemetry, never sent to the client.
""".

-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").

-include("json_rpc.hrl").

-export([dispatch/1, dispatch/2]).

-doc """
Per-request information handed to arity-2 handlers.

`connection_pid` is the transport's connection process. On the WebSocket
transport that is the pid `json_rpc_ws:push/3` and `json_rpc_ws:subscribe/2`
expect, which is how a handler talks back to its own connection.
""".
-type context() :: #{
    transport := json_rpc_telemetry:transport(),
    request_id := binary() | undefined,
    connection_pid := pid(),
    peer := {inet:ip_address(), inet:port_number()} | undefined
}.

-doc "What a transport should send back. `no_response` means send nothing.".
-type reply() :: no_response | json_rpc_response:t() | [json_rpc_response:t()].

-export_type([context/0, reply/0]).

-doc "Dispatch with an empty context. Handlers registered at arity 2 see `#{}`.".
-spec dispatch(json_rpc_json:value()) -> reply().
dispatch(Payload) ->
    dispatch(Payload, #{}).

-doc "Dispatch `Payload`, passing `Context` to any arity-2 handler it reaches.".
-spec dispatch(json_rpc_json:value(), map()) -> reply().
dispatch(Payload, Context) when is_list(Payload) ->
    dispatch_batch(Payload, Context);
dispatch(Payload, Context) when is_map(Payload), map_size(Payload) > 0 ->
    case run_all([json_rpc_request:parse(Payload)], Context) of
        [] -> no_response;
        [Response] -> Response
    end;
dispatch(_Payload, _Context) ->
    %% A bare scalar, or an empty object: not a Request object and not a
    %% batch, so there is nothing to attribute an id to.
    json_rpc_response:error(null, json_rpc_error:invalid_request()).

%%% Internal

dispatch_batch([], _Context) ->
    json_rpc_response:error(null, json_rpc_error:invalid_request());
dispatch_batch(Elements, Context) ->
    Max = json_rpc_config:get(max_batch_size),
    case length(Elements) > Max of
        true ->
            ?LOG_WARNING("json_rpc: rejecting batch of ~p (max_batch_size=~p)", [
                length(Elements), Max
            ]),
            json_rpc_response:error(
                null,
                json_rpc_error:new(
                    ?JSONRPC_INVALID_REQUEST,
                    <<"Invalid Request">>,
                    #{reason => <<"batch too large">>, max_batch_size => Max}
                )
            );
        false ->
            run_batch(Elements, Context)
    end.

run_batch(Elements, Context) ->
    Started = erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond),
    Responses = run_all([json_rpc_request:parse(E) || E <- Elements], Context),
    Duration = erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond) - Started,
    json_rpc_telemetry:batch_stop(length(Elements), Duration, Context),
    case Responses of
        [] -> no_response;
        _ -> Responses
    end.

%% Resolve every parsed element, run the ones that reach a handler
%% concurrently, then reassemble in request order. Elements that failed
%% validation never reach a worker but still hold their place in the list.
run_all(Parsed, Context) ->
    Resolved = [resolve(P) || P <- Parsed],
    Invocations = [I || {invoke, _Answerable, _Method, _Id, I} <- Resolved],
    Results = json_rpc_worker:run_many(Invocations, json_rpc_config:get(handler_timeout_ms)),
    {Responses, []} = lists:mapfoldl(fun collect/2, Results, Resolved),
    [R || R <- Responses, R =/= no_response].

%% One parsed element becomes either a ready-made answer or an invocation to
%% run. `Answerable' records whether the client is owed a Response at all:
%% a Notification is owed nothing, however the handler turns out.
resolve({invalid, Id, Error}) ->
    %% Answered even without an id — a malformed Request is not a
    %% Notification, because we cannot know it was meant to be one.
    {ready, json_rpc_response:error(Id, Error)};
resolve({notification, Method, Params}) ->
    resolve_method(false, Method, null, Params);
resolve({call, Id, Method, Params}) ->
    resolve_method(true, Method, Id, Params).

resolve_method(Answerable, Method, Id, Params) ->
    case json_rpc_methods:lookup(Method) of
        {ok, Handler} ->
            {invoke, Answerable, Method, Id, invocation(Handler, Method, Id, Params)};
        not_found ->
            answer(Answerable, json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:method_not_found()));
        {error, unavailable} ->
            ?LOG_ERROR("json_rpc: method registry unavailable, cannot dispatch ~ts", [Method]),
            answer(Answerable, json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:internal_error()))
    end.

answer(false, _Response) -> {ready, no_response};
answer(true, Response) -> {ready, Response}.

%% Build the zero-arity thunk the worker will run. Logger metadata is set
%% inside it because it is process-local and the worker is a fresh process,
%% so handler logs carry the correlation id without the handler doing
%% anything.
invocation({mfa, Module, Function, Arity}, Method, Id, Params) ->
    fun() ->
        logger:update_process_metadata(#{
            json_rpc_method => Method,
            json_rpc_id => Id
        }),
        case Arity of
            1 -> Module:Function(Params);
            2 -> Module:Function(Params, get(json_rpc_context))
        end
    end.

collect({ready, Response}, Results) ->
    {Response, Results};
collect({invoke, Answerable, Method, Id, _Fun}, [Result | Rest]) ->
    {response_for(Answerable, Method, Id, Result), Rest}.

response_for(Answerable, Method, Id, #{outcome := Outcome, duration := Duration}) ->
    Response = outcome_response(Method, Id, Outcome, Duration),
    case Answerable of
        true -> Response;
        false -> no_response
    end.

outcome_response(Method, Id, {ok, Returned}, Duration) ->
    case interpret(Returned) of
        {result, Result} ->
            json_rpc_telemetry:request_stop(Method, Duration, ok, #{}),
            json_rpc_response:result(Id, Result);
        {error, Error} ->
            error_response(Method, Id, Error, Duration)
    end;
outcome_response(Method, Id, {error, timeout}, Duration) ->
    ?LOG_WARNING("json_rpc: handler for ~ts timed out after ~p us", [Method, Duration]),
    json_rpc_telemetry:request_exception(Method, Duration, timeout, #{}),
    json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:internal_error(#{reason => timeout}));
outcome_response(Method, Id, {error, {crash, throw, {jsonrpc_error, Thrown}, _Stack}}, Duration) ->
    thrown_response(Method, Id, Thrown, Duration);
outcome_response(
    Method, Id, {error, {crash, throw, {jsonrpc_error, Code, Message}, _Stack}}, Duration
) ->
    thrown_response(Method, Id, {Code, Message}, Duration);
outcome_response(
    Method, Id, {error, {crash, throw, {jsonrpc_error, Code, Message, Data}, _Stack}}, Duration
) ->
    thrown_response(Method, Id, {Code, Message, Data}, Duration);
outcome_response(Method, Id, {error, {crash, Class, Reason, Stacktrace}}, Duration) ->
    ?LOG_ERROR(
        "json_rpc: handler for ~ts raised ~p:~p~n~p", [Method, Class, Reason, Stacktrace]
    ),
    json_rpc_telemetry:request_exception(Method, Duration, crash, #{}),
    json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:internal_error()).

thrown_response(Method, Id, Thrown, Duration) ->
    case json_rpc_error:from_term(Thrown) of
        {ok, Error} ->
            error_response(Method, Id, Error, Duration);
        not_an_error ->
            ?LOG_ERROR("json_rpc: handler for ~ts threw an unusable error: ~p", [Method, Thrown]),
            json_rpc_telemetry:request_exception(Method, Duration, crash, #{}),
            json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:internal_error())
    end.

%% A handler may not emit a framework-owned code. Substituting the internal
%% error keeps a handler from impersonating a protocol-level failure such as
%% "Method not found", which a client would reasonably act on.
error_response(Method, Id, Error, Duration) ->
    Code = json_rpc_error:code(Error),
    case json_rpc_error:is_reserved(Code) of
        true ->
            ?LOG_WARNING(
                "json_rpc: handler for ~ts returned reserved code ~p; substituting ~p",
                [Method, Code, ?JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR]
            ),
            Internal = json_rpc_error:internal_error(),
            json_rpc_telemetry:request_stop(
                Method, Duration, {error, ?JSONRPC_INTERNAL_ERROR}, #{}
            ),
            json_rpc_response:error(Id, Internal);
        false ->
            json_rpc_telemetry:request_stop(Method, Duration, {error, Code}, #{}),
            json_rpc_response:error(Id, Error)
    end.

%% Distinguish the control tuples from a plain result. Bare tuples cannot be
%% encoded as JSON, so treating them as control costs nothing a handler could
%% legitimately want.
interpret({error, Term}) ->
    case json_rpc_error:from_term(Term) of
        {ok, Error} -> {error, Error};
        not_an_error -> {error, json_rpc_error:internal_error()}
    end;
interpret({ok, Result}) ->
    {result, Result};
interpret(Result) ->
    {result, Result}.

-module(json_rpc_transport).

-moduledoc """
The decode-dispatch-encode pipeline shared by the HTTP and WebSocket handlers.

Both transports do the same three things to a payload and differ only in how
bytes arrive and leave, so the pipeline lives here and the handlers stay thin.

## Encoding is total

`encode_reply/1` never raises. A handler result that JSON cannot represent —
a tuple, a pid, a reference, a function, or a binary that is not valid UTF-8
— would otherwise take down the connection process at encode time, losing
every other in-flight call on that connection.

The fast path encodes the whole reply in one pass. Only if that fails does it
fall back to encoding element by element, so a single bad element in a batch
degrades to `-32603` on its own and its siblings are still delivered.
""".

-include_lib("kernel/include/logger.hrl").

-export([
    handle/2,
    encode_reply/1,
    error_body/1,
    error_body/2,
    request_id/1
]).

-doc "Bytes to send back, or nothing at all when the payload was Notifications only.".
-type outcome() :: {reply, iodata()} | no_reply.

-export_type([outcome/0]).

-doc """
Decode `Payload`, dispatch it, and encode the reply.

Returns `no_reply` when the payload consisted only of Notifications; the HTTP
transport turns that into `204 No Content` and the WebSocket transport sends
no frame.
""".
-spec handle(binary(), json_rpc_dispatcher:context()) -> outcome().
handle(Payload, Context) ->
    case json_rpc_json:decode(Payload) of
        {ok, Decoded} ->
            reply(json_rpc_dispatcher:dispatch(Decoded, Context));
        {error, parse_error} ->
            json_rpc_telemetry:parse_error(maps:get(transport, Context, internal)),
            {reply, error_body(json_rpc_error:parse_error())}
    end.

-doc """
Encode a dispatcher reply, degrading unencodable elements to `-32603`.
""".
-spec encode_reply(json_rpc_dispatcher:reply()) -> iodata().
encode_reply(Reply) ->
    case json_rpc_json:encode_iodata(Reply) of
        {ok, IoData} ->
            IoData;
        {error, Reason} ->
            ?LOG_ERROR("json_rpc: reply is not encodable (~p); degrading", [Reason]),
            degrade(Reply)
    end.

-doc "Encode a standalone error Response with a `null` id.".
-spec error_body(json_rpc_error:t()) -> iodata().
error_body(Error) ->
    error_body(null, Error).

-doc "Encode a standalone error Response echoing `Id`.".
-spec error_body(json_rpc_response:id(), json_rpc_error:t()) -> iodata().
error_body(Id, Error) ->
    encode_reply(json_rpc_response:error(Id, Error)).

-doc """
Take the correlation id from an upstream `x-request-id` header, or mint one.

Honouring the inbound header lets a proxy's request id follow the call into
handler logs and telemetry.
""".
-spec request_id(binary() | undefined) -> binary().
request_id(Header) when is_binary(Header), Header =/= <<>> ->
    binary:part(Header, 0, min(byte_size(Header), 128));
request_id(_Absent) ->
    binary:encode_hex(crypto:strong_rand_bytes(8), lowercase).

%%% Internal

reply(no_response) -> no_reply;
reply(Reply) -> {reply, encode_reply(Reply)}.

%% Re-encode one element at a time so the encodable ones survive.
degrade(Responses) when is_list(Responses) ->
    [$[, lists:join($,, [degrade_one(R) || R <- Responses]), $]];
degrade(Response) ->
    degrade_one(Response).

degrade_one(Response) ->
    case json_rpc_json:encode_iodata(Response) of
        {ok, IoData} -> IoData;
        {error, _Reason} -> substitute(Response)
    end.

%% The offending part is the handler's `result' (or an error's `data'), so
%% rebuild the envelope around the id alone. That is always encodable: the id
%% was itself decoded from JSON.
substitute(Response) ->
    Id = maps:get(id, Response, null),
    {ok, IoData} = json_rpc_json:encode_iodata(
        json_rpc_response:error(Id, json_rpc_error:internal_error())
    ),
    IoData.
